**Senate seat arithmetic (explicit)**

- Democratic baseline: 47 seats (incl. 2 independents), of which the contested defenses this cycle are MI, NH, GA, MN. NH/GA/MN are not in A1–A7; briefs and ratings (older than one week for some, e.g. Cook MI 14 Oct) treat them as Likely/Lean D, so model each ~0.93–0.95. MI (A3) at 0.82 is the weak defensive link.
- Needed: 51 seats = net +4, i.e. 4 GOP-held flips while holding all four defenses.
- Pickup pool from our own recommended numbers: TX 0.70, ME 0.71, OH-special 0.70, AK 0.66, KS 0.62, IA 0.48 → expected 3.87 flips from A1–A7 alone.
- **Races in play outside A1–A7:** North Carolina (the briefs' "foundational pickup," plausibly ~0.85), plus reach targets Nebraska (Osborn, I), South Carolina, Florida special, and the Democratic defenses NH/GA/MN.
- Including NC (~0.85), expected flips ≈ 4.7, median outcome 5 flips — i.e. one flip *above* the 4 needed, with Osborn/SC/FL as free options.
- Correlation cuts both ways: a uniform GOP-ward polling error of ~3–4 pts (the critics' core worry) knocks out the 0.62–0.71 cluster simultaneously and also endangers MI, so the distribution is bimodal rather than binomial-smooth. Treating the races as one shared error term, P(≥4 flips AND holding MI/NH/GA/MN) comes out around **0.68–0.75**, not 0.41.

**Verdict:** A15's own_estimate of 41.3 is flatly incoherent with A1–A7 (which imply ~4.7 expected flips) and with A14 at 95. The A15 critic's "away_from_market/structural barriers" case is already fully priced inside the individual race estimates — applying it again at the chamber level double-discounts the same GOP-polling-error argument. Market scenario split (D Senate 0.742 = 0.738 + 0.004; D House 0.941) is internally consistent and consistent with our A14. Move A15 to ~70 (recommended 68 is defensible; +2).

Other flags: A3 is pivotal for Senate control, and an 11-pt NYT/Siena lead with no fresh contrary data supports a nudge up (+1). A1's critic direction conflicts with a recommended 70 that sits *above* own_estimate 60 — the recommendation, not the critic, carries; leave at 70 for seat-math coherence. House district questions (A8–A13) sit below their markets but are individually consistent with a D+24 environment plus red-district lean; no change, noting A13's panel self-contradiction was already corrected toward market.
